brief.headline: ARTEMIS lets Claude Code drive and verify your Android app for you
brief.summary:
Google open-sourced ARTEMIS, which turns plain-language instructions into Android automation and plugs straight into Claude Code and Codex — wire it in as a verification pass and an agent can drive your app's UI end to end before you ever open the PR. Pair that with two self-verification patterns from smaller repos: fable-method's "think / act / prove" eval loop and OpenBot's pre-action gating plus action log, both aimed at the same problem, giving you something to check in the morning instead of trusting the diff.

On spend, the pattern to copy tonight is routing by task, not by vibes. A 137-document benchmark found an 8B Qwen3-VL model running locally on a laptop beat GPT-5.6 on tax-form extraction specifically, even though it lost badly on Indian date formats and trailed frontier models overall — send matching subtasks to Ollama, keep the rest on the API. Two repos let you spend an existing ChatGPT Pro subscription instead of Codex API quota for planning or execution, and a DeepSeek-based harness (dscode) adds auto-approval plus a persistent shell for cheap unattended subagent runs. Separately, OpenCode v1.18.33 fixes a real failure mode: MCP browser-launch errors now surface instead of hanging a run silently.
bullets: Clone google/artemis and wire it into Claude Code skills to auto-drive and verify Android UI flows before you review a PR
Pull Qwen3-VL 8B (Q4_K_M) via Ollama for tax-form-style extraction, it beat GPT-5.6 there; keep Indian-date-format documents on a frontier model
Route background and verification subagents to qiz029/dscode (DeepSeek, auto-approval, persistent shell) to cut token spend
Configure miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web or XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt to spend an existing ChatGPT Pro session instead of Codex API quota
Upgrade OpenCode to v1.18.33, MCP browser-launch failures now report instead of hanging a run silently
Try Sahir619/fable-method's think/act/prove eval, or CopilotKit/OpenBot's pre-action gating and action log, as a self-check step before an agent hands you a PR

signals.label: Narrow-task local models replacing frontier calls
signals.note: Qwen3-VL 8B beat GPT-5.6 on tax-form extraction on a laptop, and a 2.78T-parameter Kimi K3 now runs on a single CPU in 8.24GB RAM — task-specific routing off the API bill is getting concrete.

signals.label: Subscription-as-backend to dodge API quota
signals.note: Two separate repos (codex-chatgpt-web, codex-with-chatgpt) now let ChatGPT Web/Pro sessions substitute for Codex API spend.

signals.label: Self-verification and audit-trail patterns before PR review
signals.note: ARTEMIS, fable-method's prove step, and OpenBot's action log all target the same gap: proof an unattended run did what it claims.

signals.label: Harness and control-plane proliferation
signals.note: HarnessRouter, zeron, FrontierAgent and Fuxi all shipped competing ways to unify or replace Claude Code/Codex sessions this cycle, none yet a clear default.

items.title: Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill — Autoprompt is a coding-agent skill that cuts failures by 45% on agentic coding tasks.
items.tldr: Autoprompt, a coding-agent skill, claims a 45% reduction in failures on agentic coding tasks.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in skill that cuts agent failure rate means fewer broken overnight runs and fewer bad PRs to review in the morning.
items.tryThis: Install Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill and run it on your next unattended agentic coding task.

items.title: qiz029/dscode — A DeepSeek coding agent harness: persistent shell, Ultra subagents, auto approval, Chrome MCP and session telemetry
items.tldr: dscode is a DeepSeek-based coding agent harness with a persistent shell, subagents, auto-approval, Chrome MCP, and session telemetry.
items.whyItMatters: Auto-approval plus a persistent shell are the exact ingredients for longer unattended runs, and running it on DeepSeek instead of Claude cuts token cost.
items.tryThis: Clone qiz029/dscode, enable auto-approval, and route background/verification subagents to it to cut spend.

items.title: Qwen3-VL 8B on a laptop vs Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / GPT-5.6 on 137 messy documents: beat GPT-5.6 on tax forms, lost badly on Indian date formats[R]
items.tldr: Qwen3-VL 8B (Q4_K_M) run locally via Ollama on an M5 MacBook hit 59% full-accuracy across 137 messy documents versus Opus 89%, Sonnet 85%, and GPT-5.6 Terra 57%, but beat GPT-5.6 on W-2 tax forms and failed badly on Indian date formats.
items.whyItMatters: An 8B model on a 24GB laptop already beats a frontier model on specific document types, so matching extraction subtasks can move off the API bill tonight.
items.tryThis: Pull Qwen3-VL 8B Q4_K_M in Ollama and route W-2/tax-form-style extraction to it locally; keep Indian-format documents on a frontier model.

items.title: miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web — Use ChatGPT Web (including Pro) as a native model in Codex — with context, tools, streaming and images, without using Codex quota.
items.tldr: A new repo lets Codex use ChatGPT Web, including a Pro account, as a model backend with tools and streaming, bypassing Codex API quota.
items.whyItMatters: You can route Codex agent work through an existing ChatGPT Pro subscription instead of burning paid API quota on long unattended runs.
items.tryThis: Clone miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web and configure it as a Codex model provider to spend ChatGPT Web/Pro sessions instead of API credits.

items.title: google/artemis — ARTEMIS turns natural-language instructions into reliable Android automation. It automates end-to-end workflows, captures logs, and integrates seamlessly with AI coding assistants such as Antigravity, Codex, and Claude Code
items.tldr: Google's ARTEMIS repo turns natural-language instructions into Android automation workflows and integrates with Claude Code and Codex.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a scriptable way to have an agent drive and verify an Android app end-to-end, which is the verification step you need before reviewing a mobile PR.
items.tryThis: Clone google/artemis and wire it into your Claude Code skills to auto-verify Android UI flows before reviewing a PR.

items.title: trailhq/Graft — Turbocharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini & every coding agent: faster, cheaper, with contextual understanding specific to your codebase.
items.tldr: Graft is an open repo-indexing tool that gives Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini agents precomputed contextual understanding of your codebase.
items.whyItMatters: Cuts the grep/read cycle agents burn tokens and time on, which matters if you want an agent to spend a full unattended run coding instead of re-orienting.
items.tryThis: Install Graft in your repo and point your agent's context file at it before your next unattended run.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on a single CPU in 8.24GB of RAM using portable C99, with no BLAS and no GPU.
items.whyItMatters: A trillion-parameter-class model now runs on hardware you likely already own, removing the need for a GPU rental or cloud API bill for that workload.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and benchmark it on a spare machine with 8GB+ RAM as a free local inference option.

items.title: XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt — ChatGPT thinks. Codex works. Use ChatGPT as the planning brain while keeping the Codex harness.
items.tldr: codex-with-chatgpt wires ChatGPT in as the planning layer while execution still runs through the Codex harness.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a two-tier prompt structure — a strong model plans, a cheaper harness executes — you can copy for a Claude-planner-plus-cheap-executor setup.
items.tryThis: Clone XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt and adapt its planner/executor split to route your subagents by task difficulty.

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot — Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
items.tldr: CopilotKit's OpenBot runs each agent in its own sandboxed computer, gates every action before it happens, and logs it after.
items.whyItMatters: Pre-action gating plus a full action log gives you an audit trail to check before merging, closer to a reviewable overnight PR.
items.tryThis: Clone CopilotKit/OpenBot, wire an AG-UI agent into its sandboxed runner for one overnight task, then check the action log.

items.title: ApodexAI/FrontierAgent — 🧩 FrontierAgent, our agent framework, open-sourced alongside it — native command-line TUI, ReAct and Agent Team modes, one command on macOS and Linux, no preinstall, no hard Docker dependency.
items.tldr: FrontierAgent open-sources an agent framework with a native CLI TUI, ReAct and Agent Team modes, installable via one command on macOS and Linux with no Docker dependency.
items.whyItMatters: A self-hostable multi-agent harness alternative worth comparing against your current Claude Code + subagents setup, without the Docker overhead.
items.tryThis: Clone ApodexAI/FrontierAgent and run its Agent Team mode against a small task to compare against your current subagent setup.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: FuXi is a terminal coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across multiple LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a ready-made router for sending cheap subtasks to cheap models and reserving expensive ones for hard steps, instead of building that logic yourself.
items.tryThis: Try fuxicodex/Fuxi's provider-routing config to tier subtasks by cost instead of running everything on one model.

items.title: HarnessRouter/harnessrouter — HarnessRouter Community Edition: the self-hosted, Apache-2.0 edition of the unified interface for agent harnesses. Run Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, DSH, and more through one API, with sessions, streaming, fi
items.tldr: HarnessRouter Community Edition ships a self-hosted, Apache-2.0 API that runs Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, and other harnesses through one interface with sessions, streaming, and failure handling.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you route work across different coding-agent harnesses from one endpoint instead of scripting each separately, useful for a multi-model unattended pipeline.
items.tryThis: Clone HarnessRouter and point it at your Claude Code and Codex API keys to unify session handling.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills how Claude Fable 5 worked into reusable skills plus an eval that checks the agent's work via a "think / act / prove" loop.
items.whyItMatters: The built-in eval is a self-verification pattern you can lift directly to make an agent check its own output before handing you a PR.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and drop its "prove" eval step into your own review-before-PR skill.

items.title: acryldev/acryl — ACRYL - Agent Context Relay Yielding Lifecycles. One persistent workspace, one canonical context, any coding agent.
items.tldr: ACRYL gives any coding agent one persistent workspace and one canonical context file, instead of per-session memory loss.
items.whyItMatters: Long unattended runs across worktrees and subagents lose context between sessions; a shared context file lets agents resume correctly overnight.
items.tryThis: Clone acryldev/acryl and point your subagents at its shared context file instead of per-session state.

items.title: v1.18.33
items.tldr: OpenCode v1.18.33 makes Cloudflare AI Gateway honor timeouts, reports MCP browser-launch failures instead of hanging silently, and redacts credentials from debug output.
items.whyItMatters: The MCP failure-reporting fix directly reduces the odds of a long unattended run silently stalling on a browser MCP tool without telling you why.
items.tryThis: Upgrade OpenCode to v1.18.33 before your next overnight run.

items.title: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.
items.tldr: deepseek-harness from DeepSeek AI is a plugin-based coding agent harness, tagline "Everything is a Plugin."
items.whyItMatters: Worth checking whether its plugin architecture lets you bolt on your own verification or auto-approval plugins, the way dscode does.
items.tryThis: Clone deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness and check its plugin docs for auto-approval or verification hooks.

items.title: totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids — Cross-platform local MCP capabilities for ChatGPT with Chrome integration, Goal, Compact & Resume, and durable multi-agent workflows.
items.tldr: chat-on-steroids adds local MCP tool access, Chrome integration, and a "Goal, Compact & Resume" mechanic for durable multi-agent workflows on top of ChatGPT.
items.whyItMatters: The compact-and-resume mechanic is a concrete pattern for keeping a long agent session from blowing its context window during an overnight run.
items.tryThis: Clone totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids and study its Compact & Resume implementation for your own long-running sessions.

items.title: AlephAITech/WorkBuddyGuide — A practical, open-source guide to mastering WorkBuddy through real-world workflows.开源的 WorkBuddy 实战蓝皮书：教程、真实工作流、Skills、MCP、自动化与多智能体实践。
items.tldr: An open-source guide collects real-world workflows for skills, MCP, and multi-agent automation in a tool called WorkBuddy.
items.whyItMatters: Copyable workflow patterns for skills/MCP/multi-agent setups save you the trial-and-error of building your own from scratch.
items.tryThis: Clone AlephAITech/WorkBuddyGuide and lift its skills/MCP workflow patterns into your own Claude Code setup.

items.title: lexmount/moli — Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
items.tldr: moli is a lightweight, fast headless browser built in Rust specifically for AI agent use.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in, more compatible headless browser could unblock agent steps that drive the web during unattended runs.
items.tryThis: Swap your agent's Playwright/Puppeteer step for lexmount/moli if browser automation is a bottleneck in a run.

items.title: zeronsh/zeron — A native control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin and other coding agents.
items.tldr: zeron is a Rust control plane for running and managing Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Devin sessions from one place.
items.whyItMatters: A single control surface for multiple agent harnesses is a step toward steering overnight runs without babysitting each tool's own UI.
items.tryThis: Clone zeronsh/zeron and connect your existing Claude Code and Codex sessions to test it as a single dashboard.

items.title: SaladDay/pi-from-scratch — 600 行 TypeScript 写成的超级迷你版 pi，让你轻松从 0 写出属于你的 pi-agent
items.tldr: SaladDay published a 600-line TypeScript agent loop you can read in one sitting and fork into your own minimal coding agent.
items.whyItMatters: Seeing a full working agent loop in 600 lines shows what a harness like Claude Code does under the hood, useful if you want a stripped-down runner for background jobs.
items.tryThis: Clone SaladDay/pi-from-scratch and read the full loop end to end to see what a minimal agent harness needs.

items.title: alikon-art/DeterminFlow — A production-oriented AI workflow runtime for building, validating, recovering, and shipping complex AI workflows as dependable services. 面向生产的 AI 工作流运行时：快速开发、验证和恢复复杂 AI 工作流，并将其稳定交付为服务。
items.tldr: DeterminFlow is a runtime for building, validating, and auto-recovering AI workflows before shipping them as services.
items.whyItMatters: Built-in validation and recovery steps let a workflow catch and retry its own failures during an unattended run, instead of stalling silently overnight.
items.tryThis: Clone alikon-art/DeterminFlow and wrap one long-running agent task in its validate-and-recover pipeline before your next unattended run.

clusters.title: ChatGPT wired into Codex as backend or planner
clusters.summary: Two repos this cycle route Codex through an existing ChatGPT Web/Pro subscription instead of paid API quota, one as the execution backend, one as a planning layer above the Codex harness.

clusters.title: New DeepSeek-based coding harnesses
clusters.summary: DeepSeek AI's own plugin harness and a third-party DeepSeek harness with auto-approval and subagents both landed, aimed at running agentic coding work on a cheaper model.

clusters.title: Competing control-planes for multiple agent harnesses
clusters.summary: Four separate self-hosted tools (HarnessRouter, zeron, FrontierAgent, Fuxi) each propose a unified way to run and route across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Devin sessions.
